title: Spain Comes North
objective: After this level you can explain how Spain founded St. Augustine and New Mexico, and why the Pueblo peoples drove the Spanish out in 1680.
summary: Spain founded St. Augustine in 1565 and settled New Mexico from 1598. Po'pay's knotted cords coordinated the Pueblo Revolt of 1680, which kept Spain out until 1692.

cards.headline: In 1680, the Pueblo peoples drove a European empire out of New Mexico.
cards.body: For twelve years, Spain stayed out. The revolt came after decades of Spanish rule in the north. First: how did Spain get there?

cards.headline: Spain gets there early
cards.body: On September 8, 1565, Pedro Menéndez de Avilés founded St. Augustine, Florida, partly because France was trying to settle there too. It is the oldest continuously occupied city founded by Europeans in the United States. Out west, Juan de Oñate led settlers, priests and soldiers into today’s New Mexico in 1598, and Santa Fe became its capital in 1610.

cards.headline: Why the Pueblos rose
cards.body: Spanish rule pressed hard. Missionaries forced Catholicism on the Pueblo peoples and burned their kivas, masks and other sacred objects, and Pueblo people suffered forced labor and hunger. Po’pay, a religious leader from San Juan Pueblo (Ohkay Owingeh), had himself been imprisoned and flogged by the Spanish. He planned a revolt that needed many separate pueblos to move as one.

cards.headline: A countdown on a string
cards.body: Po’pay’s runners carried knotted cords to the pueblos. One knot was to be untied each day until the last was gone. The Spanish caught two runners, so the Pueblos struck early: on August 10, 1680, almost all of them rose together. By August 21 the Spanish had fled south toward what is now El Paso, Texas, leaving about 400 dead, including 21 priests. A piece of string had outwitted a colonial government.

mascot.line: Don’t memorize August 21. Remember the order: years of pressure, a secret countdown, a Spanish retreat.

cards.headline: Twelve years
cards.body: The Pueblos stayed free until 1692, when Diego de Vargas retook New Mexico for Spain. Twelve years is short on a timeline, and very long when you are the one who is free.

cards.headline: Spain in the north: explained
learned: Oñate took settlers into New Mexico in 1598
Po’pay’s knotted cords counted down to the revolt
The Pueblo Revolt of 1680 kept Spain out until 1692

questions.prompt: Founded in 1565, _____ is the oldest continuously occupied city founded by Europeans in the United States.

options.label: Santa Fe
options.rationale: It became New Mexico’s capital in 1610.

questions.explanation: Pedro Menéndez de Avilés founded St. Augustine, Florida, on September 8, 1565.

questions.prompt: Put these events in New Mexico in order, from earliest to latest.
items: Diego de Vargas retook New Mexico
questions.explanation: Oñate led settlers in 1598 and Santa Fe became the capital in 1610. The Pueblos struck on August 10, 1680, the Spanish fled by August 21, and Diego de Vargas retook New Mexico in 1692.

questions.prompt: The builders of Mesa Verde were among the ancestors of today’s Pueblo peoples. What did Pueblo peoples do in 1680?

options.label: Moved back into Mesa Verde’s cliff dwellings
options.rationale: Mesa Verde had been left by 1300.

options.label: Rose together and drove the Spanish out
Signed a treaty giving Spain their land
Joined the Haudenosaunee Confederacy
options.rationale: That league was in the Northeast.

questions.explanation: On August 10, 1680, almost all the Pueblos rose; the Spanish fled toward El Paso.
